remaining.title: Page numbers on the printed sheet ("page 3 of 9")
remaining.why: The running header is delivered via <thead display:table-header-group>, which is the only mechanism Chrome actually repeats. Chrome supports neither @page margin boxes nor counter(page)/counter(pages) in generated content, and a <thead> renders identical text on every page by definition, so a page number cannot come from CSS. The alternative — measuring page breaks in JS and injecting numbered markers before printing — is fragile against font fallback, paper size and the user's own margins, and a wrong page number is worse than none. Rui's two stated needs (whose wedding it is, and when this copy was printed) are both on every page now.

remaining.title: Durations with automatic downstream recalculation, and anchor-and-solve
remaining.why: The fix entry named the minimum honest version as "tap-a-row-to-edit plus 'everything from here, later by 15 minutes'", and both of those shipped. A real duration model is a different data shape (each moment gains a length, the sort becomes a solve, and every existing stored record and share link has to migrate), and doing half of it — durations that do not actually push anything — would be worse than the shift control that demonstrably moves 20 rows in one tap.

remaining.title: Per-person cards and a structured people field
remaining.why: The research's biggest unclaimed differentiator, and it is genuinely out of reach here: it needs who/where to stop being prose, a person picker on every row, a filtered view, and a batch print of one card per person. It is not in the fix list (it sits under mostWantedNext) and attempting it would have put the blockers at risk. Who/where is still one free-text line.

remaining.title: A true read-only mode for an adopted shared copy
remaining.why: Half of this landed: the copy now stamps its origin, its version and the time it was opened, so a stale copy announces itself. I did not build a locked read-only state with an explicit 'make this mine', because a recipient who genuinely needs to fix a typo on the morning of the wedding should not be blocked by a mode they have to discover how to leave, and the version stamp on screen and on paper is what actually solves the drift complaint.
